answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring diversity in who vouches for a newcomer: trust counts only when endorsers come from independent networks, providers, and histories, like a trellis that holds only if its posts stand in different soil. A thousand copies launched on one server farm, however loud their voyage across the market, collapse into a single voice, while a lone cedar grown among strangers earns real weight because its supporters cannot all be the same hand in disguise.
